title: Dillon's Box Train
about: Dillon asked for a train every time Christmas came up in conversation. What he finally got was a box train.
description: Every time Dillon was asked what he wanted for Christmas, his answer was the same: a train. No matter how many times the question came up, he never changed his mind. He wanted a train, plain and simple. But when Christmas finally arrived, the answer to his repeated request wasn't quite what he might have imagined. Instead of a traditional train, he received a homemade box train. Dillon's Box Train tells the story of how one simple, persistent Christmas wish turned into an unexpected gift and a family memory worth turning into a song.
lyrics: Verse 1
Christmas came around again,
And Dillon's name was mine,
I had a year to find a gift,
And plenty of time to decide.
So every now and then I'd ask,
What he wanted underneath the tree,
But no matter how I asked him,
He had one answer for me.Chorus
All he ever wanted was a train,
A train, a train, a train,
Every time I asked him,
The answer stayed the same.
He never said what kind he wanted,
Never gave a size or name,
All he ever wanted for Christmas,
Was a train.Verse 2
I could've bought a little model,
With a whistle and some tracks,
Or a locomotive painted red,
With a dozen cars attached.
But somewhere in my thinking,
An idea came rolling through,
He never said it had to run,
Or what it had to do.So I gathered up some cardboard,
Found some boxes I could use,
And started making something,
He'd never think I'd choose.Chorus
All he ever wanted was a train,
A train, a train, a train,
Every time I asked him,
The answer stayed the same.
He never said what kind he wanted,
Never gave a size or name,
All he ever wanted for Christmas,
Was a train.Verse 3
One box became the engine,
Another made a car,
It wouldn't travel down the tracks,
Or take him very far.
No wheels to take him rolling,
No steam to fill the air,
Just a train made out of boxes,
And a little Christmas flair.It wasn't big enough to ride,
And couldn't leave the floor,
But after asking all year long,
What could he ask for more?Bridge
I asked him in the winter,
I asked him in the spring,
I asked him through the summer,
Still the same old thing.
By the time December came,
There was no mystery,
He wanted a train for Christmas,
So a train was what he'd see!Final Chorus
All he ever wanted was a train,
A train, a train, a train,
And when Christmas finally came,

Was a train!Outro
Made of cardboard, made of boxes,
Not a single mile to gain,
But I listened to him all year long,
And Dillon got his train.Choo-choo, down the line,
A Christmas gift by my design,
He asked for one, I made it plain,
Dillon got his box train.
